blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top, every interaction with IT support is a small moment of senior communication. How a leader asks for help, how they respond when the help is slow, whether they say thank you at the end — all of this is noticed by the team on the other side, and it quietly shapes how the whole company eventually behaves.

What matters here is not what senior leaders say about culture. It is what they actually do when something small goes wrong with their laptop. A calm, specific, polite message at 9 a.m. teaches the rest of the company, silently, how to treat its own colleagues. An impatient, vague, slightly entitled message does the same — only in the opposite direction.

It is the small daily interactions with IT that set the tone for a hundred other interactions across the company. Senior leaders who understand this never complain about 'the help desk'. They communicate with humans, one small message at a time, and watch the whole culture quietly improve.

items.q: According to the text, what is 'noticed by the team on the other side'?
options: The seniority and title of the person writing
Only the technical detail of the problem
Whether the request is submitted through the correct channel
How the leader asks, responds and whether they say thank you
items.why: "How a leader asks for help, how they respond… whether they say thank you… all of this is noticed."

items.q: What does the author say actually matters for culture?
options: What leaders say about culture in formal settings
How quickly the help desk resolves tickets
The size of the IT support team
What leaders actually do when something small goes wrong
items.why: "What matters here is not what senior leaders say about culture. It is what they actually do…"

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: How help is requested matters as much as the request itself.
A small, polite message can influence company-wide behaviour.
Tone in minor interactions is essentially trivial and can be ignored.
Leaders teach culture through their everyday conduct.
items.why: Inferência: a tese inteira é que essas pequenas interações NÃO são triviais — elas dão o tom da empresa.

items.q: The phrase 'only in the opposite direction' suggests that…
options: An impatient message teaches nothing at all
IT support ignores rude messages entirely
Polite and rude messages cancel each other out
An impatient message teaches just as powerfully, but a harmful lesson
items.why: Inferência: a mensagem rude ensina com a mesma força ("does the same") — só que ensina desrespeito.

items.q: What can be inferred about a leader who 'complains about the help desk'?
options: They are being efficient with their time
They have understood the argument of the text
They are protecting company culture
They have missed the point the author is making
items.why: Inferência: quem entende a tese "never complain about 'the help desk'" — reclamar mostra que não captou a ideia.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver orientando um líder sênior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Can I show you something before your next meeting? I pulled three of your recent messages to the support team. This one just says: 'Laptop broken again. Need it fixed now.' No greeting, no detail, no thank you.

Now, I'm not raising this because the help desk complained. They didn't. What I want you to see is who else is reading over your shoulder. Every graduate on that team files your tone away, and within a month it becomes the way they write to each other.

Here is the part that surprised me. It isn't your keynote on respect that people copy. It's this nine a.m. message about a laptop. That is what they actually imitate.

So let me suggest one small change. Open with a line of context — what you were doing when it broke. Be specific about the symptom. And close by thanking them by name. It costs you fifteen seconds, and it quietly teaches a hundred people how we treat each other here. Try it this week and watch what comes back.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did Oliver bring up the leader's messages?
options: Because the leader asked for feedback on his writing
Because the help desk formally complained about them
Because the laptop kept breaking down
Not because of a complaint, but because of who else reads the tone
items.why: "I'm not raising this because the help desk complained. They didn't… who else is reading over your shoulder."

items.q: What did Oliver find surprising?
options: That the help desk never replied
That the leader wrote so few messages
That the graduates were faster than expected
That people imitate the laptop message, not the keynote on respect
items.why: "It isn't your keynote on respect that people copy. It's this nine a.m. message…"

items.q: Which three changes does Oliver recommend?
options: Call instead of writing, apologise, offer to help
Shorten the message, use bullet points, add a deadline
Copy the whole team, escalate faster, mark it urgent
Add context, be specific about the symptom, thank them by name
items.why: "Open with a line of context… Be specific about the symptom. And close by thanking them by name."

items.q: What does Oliver imply about the leader's influence on the team?
options: It only matters to the graduates, not senior staff
It spreads through small, everyday behaviour that others quietly copy
It is limited to formal presentations
It works mainly through official culture documents
items.why: Inferência: os juniores arquivam o tom ("files your tone away") e o reproduzem — a influência é pelo hábito diário.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's approach in this conversation?
options: Harshly critical of the leader's competence
Indifferent to whether anything changes
Focused purely on the help desk's feelings
Diplomatic and practical — a small, concrete fix, not a reprimand
items.why: Inferência: ele evita culpar ("one small change", "fifteen seconds") e propõe algo concreto — tom de coaching, não bronca.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The way you close a ticket is a small moment that people remember." A small moment here is…
options: a brief but meaningful interaction
a technical malfunction
a formal performance review
a scheduled meeting
items.why: Small moment = pequeno momento: uma interação breve, mas que carrega significado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A curt one-line request can sound ___ , as though the sender expects instant priority."
options: hesitant
slightly entitled
apologetic
grateful
items.why: Slightly entitled = levemente arrogante: alguém que age como se merecesse tratamento prioritário.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "His reply was so ___ that the technician had no idea which system had actually failed."
options: specific
vague
detailed
polite
items.why: Vague = vago: sem detalhe, o oposto de specific — por isso o técnico ficou sem informação.

items.q: "The tone of a leader can set the tone for an entire department." To set the tone means to…
options: adjust the volume of a call
establish the mood or standard others will follow
approve a request formally
write the official policy
items.why: Set the tone = dar o tom: definir o padrão de comportamento que os demais seguem.

items.q: "Good leaders don't just notice a delay — they respond to it graciously." To notice means to…
options: complain about something
become aware of something
escalate something
cause something
items.why: To notice = notar, perceber: tornar-se consciente de algo (aqui, o atraso).

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em contextos de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The head of IT still has to sign off on the new escalation policy." To sign off on means to…
options: comment on it casually
circulate it for reading
formally approve it
delay it indefinitely
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new support etiquette guidelines team by team." To roll out means to…
options: summarise them for the board
implement them in stages
cancel them quietly
test them in secret
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, em etapas.

items.q: "A couple of directors pushed back on the idea of thanking the help desk by name." They…
options: rewrote it themselves
adopted it immediately
forgot about it
resisted or questioned it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "He promised to change his tone, but he never followed through." He…
options: documented it badly
changed the plan halfway
failed to carry it out to completion
delegated it to an assistant
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi prometido.

items.q: "One polite message won't fix everything, but over time it does move the needle on culture." This means it…
options: costs more than expected
makes a noticeable, measurable difference
takes too long to matter
creates unnecessary friction
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, provocar uma diferença perceptível.
